title: Start here
summary: Choose your next goal: gather resources, build a workshop, survive a fight or prepare a safe return.
text: Gather stone, logs and accessible ores. Make a furnace, turn ore into ingots, then work toward powered production. Keep room in your pack for the trip home.  A small workshop supports your next expedition. Add machines as you need their outputs, then connect power, storage and conveyors rather than collecting idle equipment.  Check health, suit air and inventory space. Mark a home waypoint for navigation and a separate camp if you want a possible return point after death.

title: Mining and better tools
summary: Gather exact amounts of material and upgrade your pick to finish familiar mining jobs faster.
text: A one-metre block contains 4,096 micro-volume units, arranged 16 per edge. Small mined pieces still count: field assembly combines fractions across slots and preserves the remainder.  Collect three ordinary iron ingots. Select iron ingots in the hotbar, open the bag and press R once. A successful upgrade spends three ingots and raises pick speed from 4 to 6; pick tier stays 2. Gather at least three ordinary iron ingots. Select the iron ingots in a hotbar slot, then open the bag. Press R once; check that the upgrade succeeds and three ingots are spent. Preferred-tool stone takes 0.20 seconds instead of 0.30; iron takes 0.25 instead of 0.375. Small subvoxels still have minimum mining times. The cutter already supports tier 3, so the iron head does not unlock a new ore tier.  Start a fresh mining action after upgrading. Existing crew jobs keep the duration recorded when they were queued. The upgrade is permanent, not a separate tool item to equip or trade.

title: Fight and level up
summary: Use pulses at range, bash up close and face incoming attacks to guard.
text: In Adventure controls, hold LMB to fire pulses, press MMB to bash and hold RMB for directional guard. Face the threat while guarding. Guard blocks new shots and bash, but shots already in flight continue.  A basic pulse travels at 24 metres per simulated second for up to 24 metres, with a base firing interval of 0.20 seconds. Walls can stop shots; carved openings can let them through. Equipment changes do not change shots already fired.  Each level after the first adds 3 power to the native base of 12. Physical damage rounds once after (12 + 3 × (level − 1) + equippedPower) × (1 + damage + attackDamage). New attacks use your current level and equipped bonuses.  The documented build can disable attacks when a valid level-and-gear combination exceeds its damage limit. Unequip excessive bonuses to recover; defense and equipment management remain available. A planned correction will cap valid excessive damage instead. That correction is not part of these instructions.

title: Use abilities and supports
summary: Clear nearby enemies with a radial pulse, or change how your next pulse attack behaves.
text: Press X. The base cast has a 7-metre radius, 7-second cooldown and 1.8 damage multiplier. It selects at most the nearest 12 living targets, then checks line of sight. A wall can block a selected target without letting a farther one take its place.  In the bag, N selects None, Swift or Cascade for radial pulse. Cascade expands the maximum radius to 10.15 metres. Shift+N selects pulse support: Pierce offers up to three distinct targets at 85% per-hit damage.  An accepted cast spends its cooldown even if it hits nothing. Haste uses cooldown / (1 + haste). Changing gear or support affects the next cast, not a timer already running. These physical abilities do not cost mana or grant invulnerability.  Earlier confirmed hits can remain when a later hit fails. Do not expect every target to be hit together or the whole cast to retry. If play stops because a save outcome is uncertain, reload before continuing.

title: Collect and equip loot
summary: Claim rewards into your pack, compare their effects and equip the pieces that suit your build.
text: After an eligible kill, press P to resolve its pending reward. Regular eligible kills have a 30% loot roll. A full pack leaves the same reward pending: make space and try again, rather than expecting a reroll. There need not be a physical corpse to loot. After an eligible kill, press P to claim the pending result. If the pack is full, make space before trying the same claim again. Select the received unique item in the bag and press R to equip it. Select a unique item in the bag and press R to toggle its equipped state. Equipped pieces stay in the same 36-slot pack. Unique gear does not stack and cannot be traded or put into machines.  Press Delete twice within five seconds to confirm discarding the selected unique item. Discard gives no salvage and cannot be undone by claiming the reward again. Only supported native affixes affect play; other generated affixes remain stored on the item.  The save retains up to 1,000 lifetime unique instances, including discarded pieces, and 4,096 claims. Discarding frees a pack slot, not a lifetime instance slot.

title: Stay alive
summary: Manage health, suit condition and air separately. A larger health bar is not a refill.
text: Maximum health is 100 plus equipped life. Equipping more life increases capacity without healing or reviving you. Removing life can lower current health to the new maximum; it does not refill air or reset the regeneration delay.  Manufacture and equip the sealed helmet, hazard suit and sealed leggings. A newly completed suit starts without free air. Let it refill in breathable conditions before relying on it elsewhere.  Repair a damaged worn piece before replacing it. An empty slot or a pristine piece can accept a valid replacement. This rule prevents damaged gear from becoming pristine simply by moving through the pack.  At extremely large life values, small health changes lose precision. Keep backups and do not open high-health saves in older builds that assume a maximum of 100.

title: Build your first workshop
summary: Start with field assembly, then use fuel and power to turn raw materials into better machines.
text: Gather 8 stone and 2 logs for a Furnace. An Alloy Crucible costs 8 stone and 4 iron ingots. A Fabricator costs 4 iron, 2 copper and 2 steel ingots. These are the current provisional recipes.  Mine coal, copper and iron with starter tools. Fuel the furnace with coal to process ingots and carbon. Supply power to a crucible for steel, then to a fabricator for components and more machine kits. Gather coal and starter-accessible copper and iron ores. Fuel the furnace with coal and process the required materials. Power an Alloy Crucible to make steel, then power a Fabricator for further components. Assembly combines fractional blocks across slots and keeps leftovers. It checks output space after consuming inputs, so a slot emptied by the recipe can hold the new kit. Missing materials or insufficient space leave the pack unchanged. Unique gear is never consumed.  A running batch has already reserved its inputs. Wait for output rather than treating a preview as a finished item. Before recovering a machine, satisfy its empty, idle, fuel and energy conditions and leave room for its kit.

title: Connect power and storage
summary: Keep production supplied, move finished goods and store surplus energy.
text: Use a powered fabricator with 1 Machine Casing, 2 Control Circuits and 2 Copper Wire. The provisional recipe takes 6 seconds. Enable and power storage for automatic same-network access; manual access can remain available offline.  Workshops use local inputs first, then network storage. Outputs stay local if there is room and spill to the network when there is not. This network access is separate from goods moving on physical conveyors.  New batteries are empty. Generation charges them; capacity is 60 and charge/discharge rate is 15. To recover a charged battery, first disable it and a nearby empty battery, then use Shift+H in Build mode to transfer its whole charge. Recovery refuses a battery with positive charge.  An enabled extractor can drain buffered output to a belt even without power, but mining itself needs power. Belts cannot feed items into an extractor. Cargo Loaders connect belts and storage. Save after changing live stock or battery charge.

title: Make a breathable shelter
summary: Check the Atmosphere Unit, its power supply and filter charge before trusting a room.
text: The unit needs power, a recognized sealed room and filter charge. A visible roof alone does not establish breathability. Watch pressure and oxygen rather than assuming the enclosure is safe.  Filtering lasts only as long as the remaining charge. At most one cartridge loads at the start of a simulation tick; if charge runs out partway through, filtering waits until a later tick. Disabled or unpowered units do not provide normal filtering, and a breach vents the room.  The current room check uses cell centres, not every finest subvoxel. Small visual gaps and carved shapes may not behave as a fully detailed airtight model. A complete player-sized doorway loop is not established by this guide.  A valid camp has safe standing geometry, not guaranteed air, temperature or freedom from enemies. Save regularly; a failed ordinary save does not restore the air or filter charge used since the last successful save.

title: Give the crew useful work
summary: Designate a small job area, give workers access and check the result before expanding.
text: Aim at a whole voxel and press Shift+J to designate a 3×3 plane. Read the queued, skipped and refused counts. Existing active targets are skipped; designation does not immediately grant materials.  Provide a supported standing place, body clearance and an unobstructed approach. Workers can reach upper walls and roofs from suitable positions. A moved worker, new obstruction or changed target can stop a pending action before it spends materials.  The save holds 2,048 full work records. Explicit maintenance can archive completed or cancelled details into a ledger with up to 8,192 identities. It does not discard queued or running work to free space.  Back up the save and read the warning. Archiving permanently removes completed-job details while retaining outcomes and identities. The first archive upgrades work data to a format older builds cannot load.

title: Find your way home
summary: Use a waypoint for navigation and a separate camp for a possible return after death.
text: Stand on safe ground and press F6. The home waypoint shows direction, horizontal range and relative height on the same face. It does not teleport you or set your respawn point.  While alive on known, clear, dry ground, press F9. Shift+F9 clears the camp. Marking it does not move or heal you, grant equipment or reset cooldowns. Close gated panels and leave incompatible modes before marking. Find known, dry ground with room to stand. Close incompatible panels or modes and press F9 while alive. Check the location’s air and nearby threats; geometry alone does not make it safe. After death, the camp is used only if its exact standing position still passes same-face geometry checks. If it is obstructed or invalid, recovery falls back to the existing origin-grounding behavior. Check air and nearby threats yourself.  Dash respects collisions but does not grant invulnerability or deal damage. It does not cost mana. Do not treat dashing as protection from a dangerous landing.

title: Save and protect your progress
summary: Keep a recoverable backup, watch save results and use a compatible build.
text: A confirmed save records the changes covered by that operation. Save after ordinary movement, production and live transfers if you want those changes to survive a restart.  A known failure can leave the current world running with unsaved changes while the previous disk save remains intact. It does not undo time, production or fuel use. Transactional purchases and gear changes instead wait for confirmation before taking effect.  Stop and reload when the game reports an uncertain save outcome. Do not repeatedly retry a reward or overwrite the uncertain save. Gameplay and further saving are deliberately halted in this situation.  Keep a recoverable backup. New work archives, retired loot, item types and life-derived health may not work in older versions. Native and browser saves are not interchangeable. Cross-network multiplayer is not established by these local save rules.

title: What lies ahead
summary: Preview the wider Elysium design without mistaking future systems for current controls.
text: The intended game brings voxel exploration, action-RPG combat, loot and industry together with an optional living-colony layer in a sci-fi solarpunk universe.  Full spells and mana, expanded armor and accessory slots, trading, a broader economy, interplanetary transport, comprehensive NPC schedules and cross-network multiplayer remain separate goals rather than instructions you can follow here.  The early vehicle direction is one fixed-design amphibious rover with oversized tires that act like pontoons on water, plus one fixed starter spacecraft. Later designs are intended to be modular and player-buildable. These are planned features, not available vehicles promised by this guide.

title: How to read mechanics status
summary: Start with pages marked How to play for usable mechanics. Reference and Planned pages describe wider ideas or future work.
text: Rules and keyboard controls in this pack describe the documented documented version. Check your build’s control screen when its interface differs. Provisional values can change.  Reference is a preview drawn from the design documents or a named earlier version. Planned is requested future work. Neither label means a feature is available to use. Setting pages describe the world and its background.  A blank equipment slot is empty, not missing an imagined item. Concept layouts may show more slots than the current equipment system supports; use the actual item and control feedback.

title: Breathing, hazards and recovery
summary: Before leaving breathable surroundings, check your seal, carried air and health. Combat defense alone will not keep you breathing.
text: Breathable surroundings can replenish suit air. Crafting or equipping a suit does not fill it. When the tank runs out partway through an interval, the remaining time counts as unprotected breathing.  Heat or cold, radiation, corrosion, immersion and lava affect survival separately. Regeneration waits after damage; it is not continuous protection from hazards. Equipping more maximum health does not heal you.  A useful shelter needs a detected room, power, filter supply and suitable atmosphere. A convincing-looking enclosure is not enough, and tiny subvoxel holes are not a reliable airtightness test.

title: Home guidance versus a recovery camp
summary: Use home for directions and camp for recovery after death. They are separate markers.
text: Stand grounded in a clear position and press F6; Shift+F6 clears it. Follow its direction and height guidance to return. Home does not teleport you or set recovery. Guidance from another planet face is not a straight local route.  Setting camp does not heal, repair gear or reset combat progress. Shift+F9 clears it. Return to active gameplay controls. Stand in a clear, dry, supported position. Press F9 to mark the recovery camp. After death, the game rechecks the exact camp position on the same face. If blocked or invalid, it uses default recovery. A clear camp can still lack oxygen or contain hostile weather and enemies.

title: Mining whole blocks and subvoxels
summary: Gather only what you remove. Fine carving produces fractions of a block, which can be combined for crafting.
text: A whole block contains 16 × 16 × 16 subvoxels: 4,096 in total. Keep fractional resources rather than treating each chip as a whole block. Crew whole-cell work is different from fine player carving.  Check the target material, tool capability and pack space. A preview can become invalid if the target changes. An already-removed piece cannot provide more stock.  Not every visible plant is harvestable. Decorative groundcover is not inventory matter. Tree collision and fine harvesting are outside this version; follow the interaction feedback for your build.

title: Pack management and unique-item retirement
summary: Your pack has 36 slots. Put an item in a usable hotbar slot before trying an action that uses the held item.
text: Move or swap backpack items into hotbar slots. Fractional resources merge only up to their stack limit. Opening an item detail does not necessarily make that item your held selection.  Equipped unique gear remains the same item in your pack. The current equipment families are weapon, armor and charm; concept jewelry slots do not add usable equipment positions.  Discard also unequips the item, awards no salvage and cannot be undone or rerolled. Select the unique item you intend to remove in the bag. Press Delete once. Press Delete again within five seconds without changing selection or taking a competing action. Discard frees a pack slot but retains the item in lifetime history. That history is finite; discarding does not reset the collection limit.

title: From stone and logs to a powered workshop
summary: Start with a Furnace, smelt your first ingots, then build powered stations for steel and components.
text: The kit costs 8 stone and 2 logs. Coal fuels processing; gather ore and leave room for ingots. Open the bag with Tab, then press M for Field Assembly. Use Left/Right to choose the Furnace; press Enter once to assemble one kit. M returns to the bag; Tab closes it. Place the kit, supply ore and coal, then use the station controls to process them. An Alloy Crucible kit costs 8 stone and 4 iron ingots and needs power to make steel. A Fabricator kit costs 4 iron ingots, 2 copper ingots and 2 steel ingots. Power it to make components and further kits.  Field Assembly offers only these three starter kits. It does not produce ingots or bypass fuel and electricity. Use station recipes for later machines. These starter costs are provisional.  Check total materials and the space remaining after payment. Fractions across stacks count toward whole costs, and an emptied ingredient slot can hold the kit. Missing materials or insufficient final space leave your pack unchanged.

title: Workshop recipes, queues and blocked production
summary: Supply a station, choose its recipe and queue batches. If work stalls, check inputs, power or fuel, and output space.
text: Alt transfers whole stacks where supported. Use the controls for the station you intend to operate. Deposit ingredients with T and provide the station’s fuel or power. Select a recipe with Y/Shift+Y. Queue one batch with U or ten with Shift+U. When output is ready, withdraw with Shift+T. An active batch may already hold its ingredients while the progress bar advances. Clearing future queued work does not restore those paid ingredients or duplicate a finished batch.  Check that the station is enabled, has power or fuel, has the required inputs, and has somewhere to put output. Ingredients reserved by active work are not spare stock. A full destination can block transfer even after production finishes.  Factory work and ordinary transfers can occur before the next world save. A failed save does not rewind the running factory; reloading returns to the last saved state.

title: Iron-head pick upgrade
summary: Spend three iron ingots to mine faster with the starter pick. This improves speed, not the materials it can break.
text: The permanent upgrade costs exactly three ordinary iron ingots. A backpack focus alone is not your held source. Put ordinary iron ingots in a hotbar slot and hold that stack. Open the native bag and show the held iron detail. Press R afresh to buy the upgrade. Pick tier stays 2 and speed rises from 4 to 6. Preferred-tool stone takes 0.20 seconds instead of 0.30; iron takes 0.25 instead of 0.375. Minimum durations limit the improvement on very small chips.  Other starter tools, including the tier-3 cutter, stay unchanged. The upgrade is not a removable part or refundable swap and does not add durability or ore access. Already-prepared crew jobs keep their original duration.

title: Machine families and production roles
summary: Follow component chains to expand your workshop instead of treating each machine as a separate source of free materials.
text: Use the Furnace for fuel-dependent smelting, the Alloy Crucible for alloys such as steel, the Crusher for aggregates, the Chemical Vat for chemicals such as sealant, the Refinery for ore/concentrate processing, and the Fabricator for components and equipment.  Crusher aggregate and furnace carbon feed sealant production. Sealant then supports repair kits and composite panels, opening environmental suits and further construction.  Some stations appear as schematic footprint markers rather than solid machine models. The marker identifies a simulated machine, but is not a promise of a physical collision body or animated assembly line.

title: Provisional machine kit reference
summary: Use a powered Fabricator for these machine kits. Costs are provisional for this snapshot.
text: Crusher: 1 casing + 2 steel ingots, 6 seconds. Chemical Vat: 1 casing + 2 copper ingots, 6 seconds. Refinery: 2 casings + 1 control circuit, 8 seconds.  Conveyor: 1 steel frame + 2 copper wire, 3 seconds. Sorter: 1 steel frame + 1 control circuit, 4 seconds. Network Storage: 1 casing + 2 control circuits + 2 copper wire, 6 seconds.  Battery Bank: 1 casing + 2 copper ingots + 2 control circuits, 6 seconds. Extractor and Cargo Loader each require 1 casing + 1 actuator + 1 control circuit, 8 seconds. Newly placed batteries are empty.  Back up your world before changing builds. Older versions may not understand these kits or queued recipes; avoid downgrading after using them.

title: Manufacturing a renewable under-suit
summary: Make replacement environmental equipment at a powered Fabricator, then arrange breathable air before setting out.
text: 2 composite panels + 1 sealant + 1 copper wire → 1 Sealed Helmet in 6 seconds.  Hazard Suit: 4 composite panels + 2 sealant + 1 steel frame, 8 seconds. Sealed Leggings: 2 composite panels + 1 sealant + 1 steel frame, 6 seconds. These recipes are provisional.  Withdraw the gear, move it to a usable held slot and equip it. Repair a damaged worn piece before replacing it. New gear is pristine, but does not refill carried air; replenish in breathable conditions.

title: Environmental suits and protective layers
summary: Build a complete under-suit for a seal, then add outer protection. Environmental equipment is separate from unique combat loot.
text: Head, torso and legs each have under and over layers. The under-layer makes the seal; outer armor cannot seal an incomplete suit. Both layers can contribute thermal, radiation and impact protection.  A complete functioning under-suit can use carried air. A broken seal cannot. Applicable wear reaches outer protection before the suit beneath it, while corrosion attacks exposed layers.  Repair a damaged worn piece before swapping in ordinary packed equipment. This prevents a damaged piece from returning to the pack as pristine gear. Replacement is not a salvage operation.

title: Power demand, priorities and brownouts
summary: Keep enough generation and stored energy for your active loads. A connected machine can still be unpowered.
text: Life support and defense take priority over ordinary industry. Network Storage and Cargo Loaders use industrial power with default demand 4 and priority 4.  A load must be funded for a whole simulation step. A battery can retain a small positive charge yet fail to power that step; the leftover energy is kept.  A generator supplies energy only for the time its fuel covers. A tiny residual does not fund a full long interval. Scheduling can differ with the length of simulation steps.

title: Batteries: charging, transferring and recovering
summary: Empty a battery before packing it away. Move its charge into another battery rather than losing the stored energy.
text: A Battery Bank stores 60 energy units and charges or discharges at up to 15 power units. A newly placed bank starts empty.  Shift+H transfers the whole charge in Build mode; H recovers the empty kit. Partial combination is not supported. Disable the charged source and a nearby empty receiving battery on the same face. Stand near the source and press Shift+H to transfer its entire charge. Move near the now-empty source and press H to recover it. The receiver must be empty. Any positive source charge prevents recovery as an empty kit. Also check pack space, stored cargo, fuel and unfinished production.

title: Network Storage, conveyors and sorters
summary: Use Network Storage to supply nearby industry and belts to connect directed routes.
text: Workshops consume local ingredients first, then enabled, powered storage on the same network. Finished goods stay local if they fit; otherwise they can spill to storage. This is not a world-wide stash.  Manual deposits and withdrawals work offline. Network Storage holds 64 stacks. Read its enabled/powered flags and occupied capacity; a nearby quick-transfer action may select a different machine.  Place conveyors from source toward sink. An empty sorter passes every item type; leave a real sample in it to filter the route. Arrows show routing and state, not individual moving item models.

title: Cargo Loaders and conserving delivery
summary: Use Cargo Loaders to bridge belts and powered storage on the same network.
text: For a selected item type, the loader draws local stock before eligible remote storage. A receiving loader fills its local buffer first, then spills remotely if the local insertion will not fit.  If the sink is full, the source keeps its cargo. Recovering an empty loader does not remove connected remote stock. Sorter samples, buffers and remote storage remain separate inventories.  Automatic loading needs industrial power; manual access remains available offline. A lane can retain transfer budget while unpowered, so its first powered interval may move more than a simple two-items-per-tick expectation.

title: Automated extraction and output belts
summary: Use an Extractor for untouched, uniform natural cells. Use player mining for carved or mixed terrain.
text: Check power, placement, protection and output space. The entire natural cell must be homogeneous at subvoxel resolution. Edited, carved or mixed cells are refused rather than counted as whole blocks.  Connect a belt outward from an enabled Extractor. Stored output can drain during an outage, but producing more still requires power. An Extractor is an output-only belt endpoint: belts cannot fill it.  Disable and empty it first. Recovery may discard unpaid scan progress, not stored resources, charge or paid production. A replacement is a new machine and cannot inherit an old pending mining action.

title: Rooms, filters and breathable shelter
summary: A powered Atmosphere Unit needs a detected room and filter supply. Check the resulting atmosphere before relying on it for breathing.
text: Charge is spent by duration. With 0.01 seconds left, the unit filters for only 0.01 seconds before that supply ends; pressure and oxygen changes follow the time paid for.  At most one cartridge loads at the start of a step when needed. Disabled or unpowered units do not filter normally. A long interval does not consume unlimited cartridges to keep running.  A visual enclosure is not proof of breathable shelter. Room sealing does not reliably model every subvoxel hole, and this version has no complete doorway placement, use and recovery loop.

title: Crew mining and construction designations
summary: Mark work for citizens, then give them a reachable target and enough material. Designations do not build or mine instantly.
text: An area covers up to nine planar candidates and can accept some cells while refusing others. Construction remembers your selected material. For construction, choose the building material first. Use J for a mining target or K for a construction target. Use Shift+J or Shift+K instead to designate the corresponding planar area. The worker needs a clear supported position with line of sight within 2.8 metres of its body center. Building consumes actual material on completion, not when you mark the area.  Check the route, obstructions, body overlap, stock and target. Upper walls and roofs can be reachable, but citizens do not create scaffolding automatically. A 3×3 designation is not a guarantee that all nine jobs can finish.

title: Completed work and history maintenance
summary: Archive completed or cancelled jobs when you need room in work history. Keep a backup: archiving permanently removes their detailed records.
text: History prevents finished work from producing the same output again after reload. Both full records and archived identities have finite limits.  The confirmation pauses the game. Only finished or cancelled jobs are eligible; it awards no items or XP. In an owned native world, open the bag and press F7. Read the permanent detail-loss and compatibility warning. Press Enter to archive up to 64 terminal jobs, or Escape to cancel. Leaving it to time out also cancels. Archived jobs keep identity and final outcome, but lose detailed targets and specifications. The first archive makes work history unreadable by older builds. It is not unlimited storage, and restoring an older backup cannot restore newer history.

title: Combat: choosing an action
summary: Switch to Adventure controls for combat. Start with ranged pulses, keep room to move, and use guard or dash when enemies close in.
text: LMB fires the pulse; MMB bashes; RMB guards; Z dashes; X uses radial pulse. Build controls instead mine and place matter.  Release guard before starting a pulse or bash. Shots already in flight can still hit. Walls block attacks, including freshly edited terrain. A gap large enough for a projectile may still be too small to walk through.  Pulse and radial attacks cost no mana or ammunition. They do not apply elemental statuses or make you invulnerable. Use positioning rather than expecting an immunity window.

title: Basic pulse and projectile timing
summary: Hold LMB in Adventure mode for repeatable ranged fire. Keep a clear line to your target.
text: Each pulse travels at 24 metres per second, up to 24 metres. The base interval is 0.20 seconds; haste can shorten it. A slow frame does not bank extra shots for a later burst.  A shot checks the first living target along its path. Both the contact point and torso must be visible. An enemy hidden by terrain stops the shot; it will not skip that enemy to hit someone farther away.  A launched shot keeps its original damage and firing interval. New gear or a new level affects later shots. Entering Build or dying clears your flights; menus pause them.

title: Dash, guard and avoiding damage
summary: Use dash to reposition and guard to meet an incoming attack. Neither replaces watching the terrain.
text: Dash follows your movement direction, or camera-forward on the horizontal plane when stationary. It travels up to 8 metres with a 4-second base cooldown. Your whole body must fit. Partial movement spends the cooldown; a completely blocked dash does not.  Dash preserves vertical motion and grants no invulnerability, damage or mana cost. Landing damage happens first: dash cannot rescue a fatal landing.  Hold RMB to guard against incoming direction, not every direction at once. Guard stops new pulses and bash attacks. Stay alert after killing a ranged enemy: its already-launched bolt can still hit.

title: Melee and ranged hostile behavior
summary: Starter encounters use melee attackers. Some roaming enemies fire a delayed bolt that you can dodge after they lock their aim.
text: A ranged enemy locks aim during a 0.8-second windup. Move away from that line before its bolt arrives. The bolt travels at 10 metres per second for up to 24 metres, deals base damage 8, and is followed by 2 seconds of recovery.  Obstruction can cancel a windup. Killing or unloading the shooter before launch prevents its pending bolt, but a launched bolt remains dangerous. Reloading preserves enemy health and deaths, not its previous movement or airborne shots.  Enemies use a limited direct approach rather than elaborate routes or tactical cover. Not every roaming encounter has a ranged attacker; the wider species and boss roster is still separate.

title: Radial pulse and support choices
summary: Press X to strike nearby visible enemies. Wait until targets are in position: even a cast that hits nothing spends its cooldown.
text: The base radius is 7 metres and the cooldown is 7 seconds. Damage is 1.8 times projected physical attack damage, rounded once. The attack selects at most the nearest 12 living enemies, then checks visibility; blocked targets are not replaced with more distant ones.  In the bag, N cycles None, Swift and Cascade. Swift multiplies damage by 0.85 and cooldown by 0.75. Cascade multiplies damage by 0.85 and radius by 1.45, reaching 10.15 metres. Choose one, not both. Haste then shortens the cooldown.  The brief ring marks the accepted cast position and radius. It is not a shield or expanding damage wave. Changing support does not change a cooldown or ring already in progress.  At physical damage 12, None gives 22 damage, 7 metres and 7 seconds. Swift gives 18 damage, 7 metres and 5.25 seconds. Cascade gives 18 damage, 10.15 metres and 7 seconds. These times are before haste.

title: Pierce: trading damage for targets
summary: Choose Pierce for lined-up enemies, or None when you want full damage against one target.
text: In the bag, Shift+N changes pulse support. Pierce deals 85% damage before rounding and allows up to three distinct target opportunities per shot. None keeps a single-target pulse.  Aim through a group with clear terrain between you and the targets. The shot encounters enemies in flight order and cannot attempt the same enemy twice. A wall or obscured target ends the remaining flight.  Pulse support is saved independently of radial support. Pierce helps against a line of enemies, but its lower damage can make an isolated enemy slower to defeat.

title: Experience and level-based power
summary: Eligible hostile kills earn XP and raise the power of your next attacks.
text: A regular eligible hostile kill awards 35 XP. Reloading a saved death does not award it again. Mining and other peaceful activities do not automatically share this combat reward rule.  Projected physical damage is rounded once from (12 + 3 × (level − 1) + equipped power) × (1 + damage bonus + attack-damage bonus). Level-one base power is 12. Level gains affect new attacks, not projectiles already in flight.  In this version, an extreme gear-and-level combination can exceed the supported attack range. Change equipment to bring damage back into range; equipment management remains usable. This is not a build soft cap.  Attributes, passive allocations, profession XP, origins and callings belong to the wider progression design. They are not extra choices hidden in the current level-up system.  A planned correction would let otherwise valid attacks resolve at the safe maximum instead of becoming unavailable. Until that change is verified for your build, use the equipment workaround above.

title: Loot rolls, pending rewards and inventory space
summary: Press P to resolve one pending reward. If your pack is full, make space and try again: the reward will not reroll.
text: Regular eligible kills have a 30% drop roll. A pending item keeps its original rolls. Press P to resolve one pending reward. If the pack is full, make space without expecting a different roll. Press P again to claim the same pending item. Regular rewards are rare items with three distinct affixes: Oathblade weapons, Warden mantle armor and Astral conduit charms. Family follows the saved kill sequence. Epic four-affix boss rewards are not available through the current regular-kill route.  Pending rewards are not shared physical corpse inventories. Unique gear cannot stack, trade or go into machines.

title: Affixes: active effects and stored rolls
summary: Read which effects are active before choosing gear. Some rolled affixes are stored for future systems and give no current benefit.
text: Equipped power, general damage and attack damage improve physical attacks. Armor reduces supported physical hits, haste shortens action intervals, and life increases maximum health.  Spell damage, elemental damage, resistance, elemental penetration, critical chance, mana, recovery and penetration remain inactive. A large value in one of these fields does not make it useful in the present combat kit.  Distinct affixes have starting ranges scaled by 1 + 0.035 × (item level − 1), rounded to thousandths. Scaling a stored affix does not activate its effect.  The wider design calls for more rarity grades, contextual enemy drops and luck. The current rare rewards are not a complete common-to-SSR loot ladder.

title: Armor, haste and maximum health
summary: Choose armor to soften physical hits, haste to act sooner, and life for a larger health buffer.
text: For incoming physical damage d, armor gives d × (1 − armor / (armor + 8d + 1)); directional guard is applied through its own rules afterward. Armor does not provide elemental immunity or an airtight suit.  Supported cooldowns use base interval / (1 + haste), including pulse, bash, dash and radial. An action keeps the interval it started with, so swapping gear does not shorten a running timer.  Maximum health is 100 plus equipped unique-gear life. Adding life leaves current health unchanged. Removing life can lower current health to the new maximum. Neither action revives you.  At extremely large totals, small damage or healing may be too small for the game to represent. Do not rely on this as an immunity perk. Avoid opening such saves in older builds with lower health limits.

title: Building around the current combat kit
summary: Try these combinations as starting points, then adjust for the enemies and terrain. They are not locked classes.
text: Use None pulse support for full single-target damage. Favor active power and physical damage bonuses; haste lets you attack more often. Ignore inactive spell or critical rolls when comparing immediate benefits.  Use Pierce when enemies line up, Cascade for wider radial reach, or Swift for shorter radial downtime. All trade some damage for coverage or frequency. Draw enemies out of cover before attacking.  Combine life and armor with movement and directional guard. Carry an intact sealed suit and air for environmental survival: combat armor and life do not supply oxygen. Dash away from danger rather than through it as an immunity move.  Passive trees, elements, runes and ascension are design previews, not secret unlocks behind these supports.

title: Planets, biomes and material identity
summary: Explore for useful materials and safe places to build. Appearance alone does not tell you what a world feature does.
text: The Sixth Edition describes planet classes, temperate biomes, bounded fluid and gas behavior, and different hazards and building conditions.  The current terrain is deterministic and locally editable. This does not provide a complete seamless route across every face or between planets.  Original plant meshes, decorative groundcover and procedural trees are distinct. A visible plant does not automatically provide harvests, growth or collision.

title: Flora, fauna and contextual resources
summary: Check interaction feedback before planning food or resource supplies around a plant or animal.
text: Terrain material, harvestable matter and decorative plants do not behave alike. A rooted model alone does not supply crop growth, renewable harvests or predator-prey behavior.  The design includes crops, livestock, kitchens and fertilizer loops, with meaningful identity for named or owned animals.  Do not depend on decorative plants for supplies. Trees are not guaranteed to regrow, fall physically, seal rooms or feed industrial extractors; use only the supported interactions in your build.

title: Travel, outposts and returning to a world
summary: Use home guidance and camp recovery to explore locally. Ship travel and lasting interplanetary routes are a separate design track.
text: The Sixth Edition connects ship modules, cargo and a travel sequence. The goal is to retain cargo and identities while returning to the consequences of earlier visits.  Home guides you back; camp can choose a recovery position after death. Neither provides ship flight, interplanetary teleportation or a shared multiplayer recovery service.  Do not assume industry or citizens continue indefinitely when the application closes or a distant base unloads. Persistent saves do not by themselves provide offline progression.

title: Saving, version compatibility and safe recovery
summary: Keep a backup before changing builds, and distinguish a completed action from a completed world save.
text: New item, recipe, health and work-history features can make a save incompatible with older builds. A newer build accepting an old save does not make the reverse safe.  Some actions, such as unique-gear equipment changes and setting camp, save as part of the action. Ordinary factory production and resource transfers can run before the next world save.  When the game cannot tell whether a save completed, it stops further changes and saving. Reload the world to recover the recorded result instead of repeatedly trying the reward or overwriting it.  Restoring an older backup removes changes recorded after it. The game cannot reconstruct that lost history, and local save protections are not online anti-cheat.

title: Multiplayer and network expectations
summary: This guide describes local mechanics. It does not establish separate-network co-op availability.
text: Network Storage connects inventories within a base network. It does not connect another player over the internet or grant access to someone else’s pack.  Building permissions, trade ownership, shared claims, offline bases and synchronized travel need multiplayer rules of their own.  Check the release information for the build you will use. Local saves and a working menu are not proof of internet multiplayer or physical-controller compatibility.

title: Life skills, professions and practice
summary: Design preview: practical professions would develop through everyday work and connect your character to settlement life.
text: The Sixth Edition groups skills around extraction and construction, metallurgy and fabrication, utilities and maintenance, agriculture and food, medicine, knowledge, administration and social work, combat, and art and culture.  Practice would improve skills with diminishing returns, supported by mentorship, guilds, libraries and drills. Injury, stress and poor tools could reduce performance without erasing learned rank. A profession would not forbid all other work.  Mining, crafting and crew work are available foundations. Full profession XP, institutions and their progression feedback are not available through every activity yet.

title: Sockets, reforging and ascension
summary: Design preview: customize an existing item through sockets, reforging and ascension rather than replacing it with an unrelated item.
text: The reference separates inventory crafting, fabrication, powered processing and item-preserving workstations. Sockets, reforging and ascension belong to that last category.  The Sixth Edition describes sockets based on tier, a 1.75× bonus when rune and item elements align, and no duplicate rune ID on one item. These are reference rules, not instructions for a currently usable station.  The current unique-gear loop offers claim, equip and discard, not a complete socket, reforge or ascension workflow. Discard gives no salvage; do not destroy an item expecting materials for one of these future systems.

title: Profession catalogue: reference names
summary: Earlier-version reference: eleven named disciplines give a preview of the profession system’s vocabulary.
text: Crystallography, Mineral extraction, Xenoforestry, Xenobotany, Aquaculture and Planetary survey cover resources and environmental knowledge.  Metallurgy, Biochemistry, Field nutrition, Systems salvage and Systems fabrication cover making supplies and maintaining an expedition.  These names come from the archived browser progression catalogue. They are not eleven active skill bars in the current native game; fishing, plant growth, scanning XP and profession bonuses are not implied by their names.

title: Passive trees and named ability reference
summary: Earlier-version reference: the browser catalogue offers a preview of broader ability and passive-tree ideas.
text: Crescent cut, Astral lance, Halo rupture, Rift step and Seraphic eclipse appear in that catalogue. The current radial and dash borrow selected ideas, but the free basic pulse is not the full Astral lance ability.  Blade, arcane, ward, precision, vitality and artisan foundations lead into named ideas such as Crimson covenant, Archmage, Iron resolve, Perfect fracture, Living wellspring and Master artisan. These are not currently allocatable native nodes.  The earlier reset rule returns allocated passive points without granting extra earned points. It is not a current native reset button or attribute-allocation menu.

title: From work crews to a settlement society
summary: Design preview: grow a settlement with institutions, supplies and social responsibilities beyond individual work orders.
text: Public halls, shrines, guildhalls, libraries, hospitals, memorials, assemblies and barracks would need people, rooms, supplies and obligations to function.  Hospitals would provide diagnosis, treatment, recovery supplies and reservable beds. Memorials and archives would preserve ownership, authorship, cultural associations and important events.  Crew mining, construction and work history are available. Full relationships, daily schedules, staffing, justice and medical treatment are not yet part of that work-order loop.

title: Economy, trade routes and social consequences
summary: Design preview: production would feed markets, contracts and trade routes with local consequences.
text: Markets would react to goods available; caravans would carry manifests along routes; contracts would track objectives and deadlines. Trade would change ownership and relationships.  Weather, threats and political suspicion would influence trade. Diplomacy would matter alongside cargo capacity and price.  Storage, belts and Cargo Loaders move local industrial goods. They are not player markets, auctions, shop management or interplanetary trade. Unique gear cannot currently be traded or deposited in machines.

title: Early vehicles: amphibious rover and starter spacecraft
summary: Planned first vehicles: one fixed-design amphibious rover and one fixed-design starter spacecraft.
text: The rover is intended to use oversized tires and pontoon-like flotation. It is one amphibious ground vehicle, not a separate rover and boat.  The other first vehicle is a basic pilotable spacecraft. Later versions are intended to become fully modular and player-buildable.  You can’t drive either in this version. Acquisition recipes and a release date are not yet established.

title: Ground vehicles: rovers, crawlers and mining rigs
summary: Design preview: scout rovers, cargo crawlers and mobile mining rigs would serve different surface journeys.
text: A fast survey vehicle with light cargo. Terrain vulnerability is part of the tradeoff: speed would not remove every slope or obstacle.  A slow bulk hauler intended to benefit from roads and bridges, linking extraction sites to bases or landing pads.  A power-hungry mobile drill or extractor whose activity could attract political suspicion. It is distinct from the stationary Extractor kit.  This snapshot has no established driving controls or acquisition recipes. The early fixed-design rover and spacecraft are planned first steps; the wider vehicle roster remains a preview.

title: Modular ships and expedition preparation
summary: Design preview: prepare an expedition by balancing range, cargo, protection and utility modules.
text: Warp Drive I–IV, Pulse Engine, Atmospheric Thrusters and Vector Jets are reference modules. Fuel, cargo and handling would constrain routes and discrete jump ranges.  Fuel Tanks, Cargo Racks, Survey Scanners, Deep Scanners and Atmosphere Samplers support exploration. Hull Plating, Thermal Shields, Radiation Baffles, Autopilot, a Navigation Core and Emergency Beacon support travel safety. Autopilot would assist rather than remove hazards.  Docking Collars, Drone Bays, Habitation Pods, a Small Refinery and Smuggler Hold are proposed modules. Field processing would be less efficient; reduced inspection exposure would trade away cargo efficiency.  Continuous travel without a loading screen is a design goal, not a route currently available through home guidance or camp recovery.

title: A universe beyond the next ridge
summary: Explore a frontier of ancient institutions, independent communities and worlds shaped by long silences.
text: An ancient interstellar empire spans worlds shaped by long periods without its ruler’s direct oversight. Separate powers and identities grew in those silences. Its return brings questions of cooperation, independence and rebuilding to a galaxy that has never had just one culture.  Elysium brings that wide setting down to an explorer’s scale: a route through unfamiliar terrain, material worth carrying home, and a shelter that makes the next journey possible.  The frontier’s communities have purposes beyond the passing explorer. Independent institutions, places of work and relationships between settlements give an inhabited world its history and its reasons to endure.

title: Worlds and places
summary: Get to know Epsilon-7, Bellwynn and Caldris II: places of civic life, cultivation and industry.
text: Epsilon-7 is the Imperial capital, home to the Citadel and major institutions. It establishes the setting’s contrast between immense, durable civic infrastructure and the smaller outposts from which an expedition begins.  The geographic register associates Greenhaven on Bellwynn with a harvest and innovation festival, and Caldris II with industrial and agricultural development. They offer grounded examples of everyday cultivation, engineering and community life rather than only battles and imperial monuments.  A base is more than a container for possessions. Paths connect useful rooms, machinery serves a task, and living space has a purpose. The distinction between a temporary camp and a place worth returning to lies in how those parts work together.

title: Work, trade and industry
summary: Meet the organizations behind the setting’s mining, shipping and advanced manufacturing.
text: Somnus is a private commercial group overseen by Lethe. Wheatley Storage & Shipping handles logistics; SMITE expands to Space Mining and Industrial Technology Expeditions; Apophatic Technologies develops advanced industrial processes. Their names describe distinct roles, not interchangeable labels for all industry.  Bellweather is an independent cooperative with a nonexclusive relationship to WSS, not a subsidiary. Imperial public institutions and private Somnus holdings remain separate: ownership, contracts and cooperation are different kinds of relationship.  Mining, crafting, storage and automation form a chain of practical work. A component matters because it helps make, carry or maintain something; a workshop turns raw material into a reason to undertake the next journey.

title: Technology with a living purpose
summary: Read the frontier’s engineering through enduring structures, living greenery and carefully made machines.
text: Utility and beauty belong together in the setting’s technology. Distributed systems, automated maintenance and self-repairing infrastructure describe an engineering culture concerned with endurance as well as invention.  Visible connections, useful light, clear controls and accessible machinery make the built world legible. Vegetation and living space coexist with engineering rather than being pushed outside it.  Warm gold emphasizes craft; cyan and teal make technical information clear. Pale ceramic surfaces suggest precision equipment, while living green connects that equipment to the world around it. Together they form Elysium’s solarpunk visual vocabulary.

title: Equipment with identity
summary: Discover why an item’s name, craftsmanship and history can matter as much as its appearance.
text: Ordinary equipment, grades, forging and exceptional named relics occupy different places in the armory. A useful item can carry a story through its design and role, long before it becomes famous.  Aletheia is an exceptional named weapon, not a generic starter spear. Its distinctive identity provides a reference for signature equipment: an object recognizable by more than its statistics.  In play, the current item’s displayed values and supported effects determine its function. Appearance communicates identity; equipment statistics describe what it can actually do.

title: Setting glossary
summary: A quick reference to the places, organizations and calendar of Elysium’s world.
text: Epsilon-7: the Imperial capital. Citadel: a central institution and landmark there. ICE: Imperial Concord Era, the source setting’s calendar designation.  Somnus: a private commercial group. WSS: Wheatley Storage & Shipping. SMITE: Space Mining and Industrial Technology Expeditions. Apophatic: advanced industrial research. Bellweather: an independent cooperative, not a Somnus holding.  Follow the frontier guide for the wider history, the industry guide for commercial relationships, or the armory guide for the identity of equipment. For controls and usable effects, turn to the linked player guides.

title: Sources and versions
summary: Curated provenance and implementation status for this mechanics edition.
text: The mechanics summaries were reviewed on 18 November 2026 against native development documentation. These are editorial summaries, not a published source-code audit, verified Windows release manifest or promise of availability in an installed build. Internal development notes are not republished here. The public Sleeping Empire repository is the existing website source. Its browser adaptation has a public port audit, linked below. That audit describes browser rules and their lineage, not proof of native feature parity. Public reference links do not independently substantiate every native detail in this edition. How to play covers the documented native version, not a guarantee for every installed build. Reference explains a design or rule set. Planned previews unavailable features. Setting describes the world and its narrative. Sections with a different status carry their own label. Reconcile each summary against the current implementation before changing its status. Keep controls, compatibility limits and provisional balancing explicit. Publish only curated mechanics material, not raw internal engineering records.
